title: fix(prompts): teach only view keys a real renderer answers, and gate it
body:
Fixes #8929

## The measurement that decided the shape

The card names two retired keys on the List Views **Keys** bullet. Both obvious corrections were measured first, and both fail:

- **Delete the two names.** That is the option triage rejected — a hand list that has drifted once drifts again.
- **Re-derive from the registry.** Measured on `a92eef266`: the generated `known-schema-types` list still carries **both** `view:kanban` and `view:gantt`. They are members of `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS`, and `registerPlaceholder` is a real `ComponentRegistry.register(...)` call, so the registry answers them — with the opt-in placeholder panel. Re-deriving from "what resolves" is a **no-op** on this defect.

So the two sets are named and separated:

| question | population | who asks it |
|:--|:--|:--|
| what RESOLVES | every registered key, placeholders included | `objectui check` — which is why a document naming a retired key validates green and draws nothing |
| what is AUTHORABLE | keys some site OTHER than the placeholder module registers | a prompt teaching an author |

## What landed

**`scripts/check-prompt-component-keys.mjs`** (new, `pnpm check:prompt-keys`) — every key on a `**Keys:**` bullet under `.github/prompts/**` must be answered by a real renderer.

The key universe is the shared `deriveRegistryKeys` — the same derivation that judges doc snippets and generates the CLI known-type list — which records, per key, the **sites** that register it. The exclusion comes from the placeholder module's own declaration in `INDIRECT_REGISTRATIONS` (now exported for this): the entry that declares the `protocol-placeholder` namespace names the module, and a key whose every site is that module is placeholder-only. **No list of key names is written down anywhere in the gate** — such a list is precisely the drift this card exists about. Move a key out of `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS` into a real plugin and the gate follows it live.

Three refusals rather than a pass, because an exclusion that excludes nothing collapses the gate back into the generous question: no declaration naming the placeholder namespace, an exclusion that removes no keys, and a prompt surface with no `Keys:` bullet left.

Completeness is deliberately **not** checked — the bullets end in `etc.`, so the file claims examples, not an enumeration. Gating the other direction would red on every plugin that ships.

**`.github/prompts/component.prompt.md`** — the corrections, plus one note saying the thing the file never said:

- List Views: `view:kanban` / `view:gantt` → `object-kanban` / `object-gantt`, the surviving spellings.
- Form Views — the second `Keys` bullet, which the card does **not** mention: the gate found `view:wizard`, `view:tabbed` and `view:drawer` placeholder-only there too. That bullet is now `view:simple`, `view:form`, `view:detail`, with a sub-bullet recording that `tabbed` / `wizard` / `split` / `drawer` / `modal` are a `formType` prop on `view:form`, not registry keys of their own.
- A note under **View Layouts**: a `Keys` entry is a REGISTRY key, a `Required Types` entry is a spec `type` value, and they have diverged. `{ "type": "kanban" }` in a `ListView` config is spec-valid; the board component is registered as `object-kanban`.

**Wiring** — a step in the existing Doc Component Types workflow, which has exactly this blind spot already: `ci.yml`'s type-check diff excludes `'**/*.md'`, and `.github/prompts/**` is nothing but `.md`. That workflow's header invites additions that need no install; this gate reads the checkout with `node:fs` and imports one sibling gate, and the wiring test walks the whole import graph to keep that true.

⛔ Nothing was changed to make the prompt true: `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS` is untouched, the generated known-type list is untouched, and the retirement pins in `plugin-kanban` / `plugin-gantt` are untouched.

## Ablation — both directions, restored by hash

Run on the committed tree, each leg proved to have landed on disk before the result was read, both files restored by `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` and verified by blob-hash equality against `HEAD` (`git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards).

| leg | mutation | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| baseline | none | `exit 0` — "Every key taught on a `Keys:` bullet is answered by a real renderer" |
| A | the corrected List Views bullet reverted to `view:kanban` / `view:gantt` | **`exit 1`**, 2 findings, both `placeholder-only-key` |
| B | leg A's prompt, plus the gate's placeholder exclusion neutralised so every registered key counts as authorable | **`exit 0`** — authorable count `536` → `650`. This is "re-derive from the registry" reproduced as code: green on the defect. |
| restore | — | blobs equal `HEAD`, gate back to `exit 0` |

Leg B is the one that matters: it demonstrates the exclusion is load-bearing and that a gate built on the obvious reading would have passed the very keys this card is about.

## Gates run

| gate | printed verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `node scripts/check-prompt-component-keys.mjs` | `OK  Every key taught on a Keys: bullet is answered by a real renderer.` — 3 prompt files, 2 bullets, 8 taught keys against 536 authorable (650 registered less 114 placeholder-only) |
| `pnpm check:doc-types` | `✅  Every documented component type is registered.` — 188 doc files, 896 `type` literals, 650 registered keys |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` — 4 files changed, 0 published source, 0 changesets added ⇒ **none owed, none added** |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0` |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | `✅  check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 7290 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `pnpm check:entry-guard` | `✓ check:entry-guard: 87 scripts/ file(s) — no entry guard outside the baseline` |
| `pnpm check:skills-paths` | `✅  check-skills-paths: OK (88/89 stated path(s) resolve across 20 guide file(s); 1 baselined).` |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test <the six changed paths>` | `✅ NOT GOVERNED — 6 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.` |

**Tests** — `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/` on the final commit: `Test Files  141 passed | 2 skipped (143)`, `Tests  4189 passed | 2 skipped (4191)`, exit 0. The new suite is 17 cases, every one driving the real derivation over a throwaway tree.

**Lint — declared narrowing.** `eslint --no-inline-config` was run over the 3 changed JS/TS files rather than the repository (`--format json`: 3 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings). The narrowing is a measurement, not a skip: `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting (no `projectService`, no `parserOptions.project`), so no rule's verdict on an untouched file can move because of this diff. CI runs the repository-wide pass.

## Found and NOT done

Filed bare as #9098: the same defect class lives in five more places in this same file — `atom:*` (six keys, nothing registers any of them), `ai:chat_window` (deliberately unregistered), `user:profile` (retired from `PageComponentType`), and placeholder-only `ai:*` / `nav:breadcrumb`. Those bullets are labelled *Required Library* / *Required Components*, not *Keys*, and what that label claims — roadmap or registry vocabulary — is a decision, not a mechanical fix. Correcting them here would have widened this PR past its ruling.

Triage's recorded **register gap** (`.github/prompts/**` steers every AI contributor yet is not in `GOVERNED_SURFACES`) was deliberately left alone: it belongs to the skills lane and was not this card's.
